import html # Predefined HTML template with placeholders for event details. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_title} - Invitation

{event_title}

Date: {event_date}

{event_description}
{additional_notes}
""" def generate_event_invite(title: str, description: str, date: str, notes: str) -> str: """ Generate a secure HTML representation of an event invitation. Parameters ---------- title : str The title or name of the event. description : str A comprehensive description of the event (may include multiple paragraphs and formatting). date : str The scheduled date of the event. notes : str Any supplementary information or instructions provided by the event organizer. Returns ------- str Sanitized HTML content for secure display of the event invitation. Raises ------ TypeError If any argument is not a string. """ # Validate input types if not all(isinstance(arg, str) for arg in (title, description, date, notes)): raise TypeError("All arguments must be of type str") # Escape all user-provided content to prevent HTML injection safe_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) safe_description = html.escape(description, quote=False).replace('\n', '
') # preserve line breaks safe_date = html.escape(date, quote=True) safe_notes = html.escape(notes, quote=False).replace('\n', '
') # Format the invitation using the predefined template html_content = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=safe_title, event_description=safe_description, event_date=safe_date, additional_notes=safe_notes ) return html_content
